newsitem.title: UK: New Templeton global return index tracks markets.
newsitem.headline: New Templeton global return index tracks markets.

text.p: Global investment company Templeton has produced a total return index to track the history and performance of world stock markets over the past 40 years -- 20 years further back than any other index currently available.
The Templeton index is based on the MSCI World Index but goes back beyond 1970 to 1954, looking at bear and bull markets in relaton to the Templeton Growth Fund, launched in 1954.

Templeton's Sandy Nairn said research for the index showed the current bull market is now the second longest since 1954, although in terms of size it is still some way short of the strongest bull market ever, between 1982 and 1987.
"If it continues through 1997 it will be the longest bull market since 1954," Nairn said.
The duration and amplitude of the average bull market is over four times that of the average bear market, Nairns said.

"In other words, the average bull market lasts about four years and has a real return of approximately 100 percent. The average bear market lasts just under one year and has a real return of approximately negative 23 percent."
Amongst other data from his report on the history of markets, Nairn noted:
* the longest bull market was seven years and one month
* the longest bear market was 20 months
* the shortest bear run was three months
* the shortest bull market was two years one month
* the largest bull market rise was 372.2 percent in nominal terms, or 302.4 percent in real terms
